questionText:
Statements:
• All cats are animals.
• All animals have hearts.
Conclusion: All cats have hearts.
explanation: All cats → animals → have hearts. Therefore all cats have hearts. ✓

questionText:
Statements:
• Some birds can fly.
• All birds are animals.
Conclusion: Some animals can fly.
explanation: Some birds can fly, and all birds are animals → some animals can fly. ✓

questionText:
Statements:
• No dogs are cats.
• All cats are mammals.
Conclusion: No dogs are mammals.
explanation: Dogs may still be mammals through another path. 'No dogs are cats' doesn't mean no dogs are mammals. ✗

questionText:
Statements:
• All roses are flowers.
• Some flowers are red.
Conclusion: Some roses are red.
explanation: The red flowers may not include roses. This conclusion does not necessarily follow. ✗

questionText:

Conclusion: All mangoes are healthy.
explanation: Mangoes → fruits → healthy. All mangoes are healthy. ✓

Conclusion: All students succeed.
explanation: Only 'some' students are intelligent, so not all students necessarily succeed. ✗

explanation: The rich graduates may not be doctors. Conclusion does not follow. ✗

• All B are C.
• All C are D.
Conclusion: All A are D.
explanation: A→B→C→D. Therefore all A are D. ✓

questionText:

explanation: Politicians are liars, but the wealthy liars may not overlap with politicians. ✗

questionText:

Conclusion: Some animals are not dogs.
explanation: Cats are animals but no cats are dogs → some animals are not dogs. ✓

explanation: Only 'some' intelligent are honest; teachers may not be in that subset. ✗

Conclusion: No sparrow is a fish.
explanation: Sparrows→birds→wings, and no winged creature is a fish → no sparrow is a fish. ✓
